summary: Pham Thi Tuyet Tam specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, supervised by Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (both attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served at the University of Chicago (1963–1978), Harvard University (1978; 1980–1986), and as director of the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious studies who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. Attested in 2010, he served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip Boas Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his bachelor's and PhD from Columbia University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya. From 1968 to 1996, he was Adjunct Associate Professor and East Asian Library librarian at Columbia.

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from around 1989 to 1996. Around 2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.
Philip Deslippe specializes in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2020, he completed his PhD and served as a teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Daiun Harada, and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (~1971–1985) and the University of Notre Dame (1985), and served as president of the American Philosophical Association (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a B.A. at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies figure who earned a BA from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker (1972–1987). He was head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984), abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991), and a resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo.

Philipp A. Maas works in Indology and philosophy, earning his PhD from the University of Bonn (–2004) under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He has held posts at Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Leipzig.

Philippe Stern was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments at the Musée de la parole et du geste (around 1928), the École du Louvre (1929–1965), and the Musée Guimet (1927–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2010, he earned his PhD at McGill University under doctoral supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and also studied with Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Richard P. Hayes, among others.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of Tibetology at INALCO starting in 1842 and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1857 to 1894.

Phillip E. Bloom works in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. Attested in 2013, he completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned B.A. degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. Attested in 2012, he served as Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University's Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector.

Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), Buddhist Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1999), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. Attested in 2013, he served as an Associate Professor at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
